reasons: Detection is sound: Section 17(b) gives Sparkling a convenience exit but only at 90 days' notice with no refund of prepaid fees, which sits at the playbook fallback rather than the preferred 30-day/pro-rata-refund position; the vendor-side limb is correctly assessed as compliant (Garman's termination rights are limited to insolvency/uncured default).

Redline is directionally correct and reaches the preferred position with a targeted edit: notice reduced to thirty (30) days in both places it appears in 17(b), 'for convenience and without penalty or early termination charge' clarified, and a pro-rata refund of prepaid (including maintenance) fees added, tracking the model language. Surviving certification/cease-use obligations are preserved.

The failed 'Customer convenience termination present' check appears to be a phrasing-variant miss — the operative sentence does read 'Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time, in whole or in part, for convenience' — and the 0.434 changed-character ratio is explained by the two notice-period substitutions plus the appended refund sentence, so neither undermines the edit.
Comment is accurate, concise, in-house voice, correctly cites the playbook position, and offers the sensible 60-day fallback conditioned on retaining the refund.

Severity suggested down to medium: the clause already satisfies the fallback (customer right at 90 days, no vendor convenience right), so the residual gap is preferred-vs-fallback (notice length and refund) rather than a walk-away breach.
